market_brief: The AI-hardware unwind that hit Wall Street on Tuesday (SOX -7.9%, Nasdaq 100 -2.0%, while the Dow held above 50,000) spread hard into Asia: Kospi fell about 5.6% and Taiwan over 6%, with SoftBank, Kioxia, Samsung and SK Hynix down 9-16%. India bucked the trend, with the Sensex up more than 2% by midday on a rebound from Monday's expiry-led drop. Rate-hike pricing is the other driver: the US 10Y sits near 4.90%, Williams says he is open to back-to-back hikes, and gold (-2.6%) and silver (-5.7%) slid as traders braced for today's October PCE and Q3 GDP. US futures point lower (Nasdaq 100 about -1.4%) ahead of the data and Thursday's Thanksgiving close, and the Bank of Korea decides on a possible hike on Thursday.
ai_brief: AI's capital-markets story turned sour: Anthropic closed below its $83 IPO price for the first time and the WSJ reports OpenAI has pushed its own listing to 2027. On the research side, a Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof certified in Lean is drawing both attention and pushback, and OpenAI posted an unreviewed matrix-multiplication preprint. Open-weights releases continued from MemTensor and Tencent, while policy news centred on Character.AI's contested asset sale and a two-year extension of UN autonomous-weapons talks.

items.headline: Asian chip stocks tumble: Kospi down about 5.6%, Taiwan over 6%, Nikkei 3.6%
items.summary: The AI-hardware selloff from Wall Street spread across Asia, with TSMC down about 8% and MediaTek 10%. Hong Kong was the exception, gaining about 1%.

items.headline: SoftBank, Kioxia, Samsung and SK Hynix lead the Asian slide
items.summary: SoftBank fell about 16% and Kioxia about 15%, while Samsung and SK Hynix dropped 6-9%, extending Tuesday's US memory rout in Micron and SanDisk (each about -11%). The Kospi broke below 5,000.

items.headline: Sensex jumps over 2% to about 84,350 at midday, defying the Asian rout
items.summary: Nifty traded near 25,900 as banks and insurers rallied, with ICICI Bank at a record high; the move reverses Monday's expiry-led slide. APL Apollo sank about 20% to a 52-week low, and Cipla rose on a US FDA generic approval.

items.headline: US futures slide again before the PCE/GDP data dump; Nasdaq 100 futures down about 1.4%
items.summary: Futures extended Tuesday's tech losses in early Wednesday trade; the S&P fell 0.5% on Tuesday while the Dow rose 0.85%. Retailers Kohl's and Dick's each jumped more than 15% in the prior session.

items.headline: NY Fed's Williams says prices are too high and won't rule out back-to-back hikes
items.summary: Williams expects inflation near 3.5% at end-2026 and back at 2% only in 2028, citing Middle East energy and chip shortages. CME pricing showed about 93.5% odds of 25bp on Dec 9 and roughly 6.5% for 50bp.

items.headline: Australian October CPI runs at 4.9% y/y, above expectations, adding pressure on the RBA
items.summary: The hotter-than-forecast reading raises the risk of a further RBA hike after four increases this year. The ASX 200 slipped about 0.5%.

items.headline: Bank of Korea meets Thursday; DBS expects a 25bp hike to 3.25%
items.summary: DBS calls the decision close, noting October minutes in which most members favoured tightening and CPI at 2.8%. Today's equity rout adds a complication for the board.

items.headline: BNP Paribas downgrades Micron to Neutral and cuts its target to $775 from $1,700
items.summary: The analyst now sees DRAM/NAND supply and demand balancing by mid-2027, earlier than before. Micron fell about 11.5% on Tuesday and sits roughly 48% below its peak.

items.headline: After-hours: Amcor drops 14%, Waters and Penumbra about 11%; ESCO jumps 13%
items.summary: Thin pre-holiday liquidity amplified post-close moves on results. After-hours decliners outnumbered advancers.

items.headline: Gold falls about 2% and silver 5% as traders price a December Fed hike
items.summary: Spot gold dropped to about $3,557 while platinum and palladium lost about 4-5%, with forced selling to meet margin calls adding pressure. JPMorgan still sees $4,500 by end-2027.

items.headline: Oil eases about 1% as surplus expectations outweigh Middle East risk
items.summary: Brent and WTI slipped in Asian trade, giving back part of Tuesday's rebound, even after a Houthi attack on Riyadh's PIF tower. WTI is near $81.

items.headline: Update: Schumer calls for congressional probes of Nvidia; SEC reportedly reviewing disclosures
items.summary: Trump said a pardon for Huang is 'always an option'. Nvidia fell another 2% after hours following Tuesday's ~6% drop, and Polymarket put a higher S&P open at only 38%.

items.headline: US adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist over alleged Nvidia chip exports to China
items.summary: The entity listing targets alleged diversion of advanced Nvidia accelerators, per BBC reporting summarised in the digest.

items.headline: SpaceX slips back below its $135 IPO price; Tesla names committees for a possible merger
items.summary: Five independent directors will sit on special committees, and Bloomberg reportedly says a Tesla-SpaceX deal could come as early as December. Musk says most of SpaceX's AI revenue comes from GPU rental.

items.headline: Bitcoin near $59,000-60,000 as November losses revive 2022 bear-market comparisons
items.summary: Bitcoin is down as much as 23% in November, per the report, as rate-hike pricing and the tech selloff weigh on crypto. Ether is below $1,700.

items.headline: Today: October PCE, Q3 GDP, durable goods and claims at 8:30 ET; Beige Book; Deere results
items.summary: Consensus is about +0.3% m/m for core PCE, about 3.4-3.5% for revised GDP and roughly 201k claims. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, with the Bank of Korea deciding the same day.

items.headline: Anthropic closes below its $83 IPO price for the first time, five days after listing
items.summary: The stock fell about 6.5% on Tuesday as AI shares sold off and is now down sharply from its debut peak. Analysts remain largely positive, per reports.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly pushes its IPO to 2027
items.summary: Per a WSJ report summarised by Wisevoter, OpenAI will list next year after Anthropic's debut. It is valued at about $1.25 trillion after an $11bn raise.

items.headline: Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof certified in Lean, but critics push back
items.summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude helped produce the proof in about six weeks, and Lean FRO and Mathlib certified 17 million lines of Lean on Nov 21. A mathematicians' group calls it unreadable publicity.

items.headline: OpenAI preprint claims the matrix-multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4
items.summary: The unreviewed claim, posted in OpenAI's math repo, includes a matching lower bound, though only a narrower case is Lean-formalised. Independent verification is pending.

items.headline: Anthropic puts MCP server Skills into public beta; Tasks and Elicitation reach GA
items.summary: The update lets MCP servers ship skills alongside tools and makes long-running tasks and structured user prompts generally available.

items.headline: MemTensor open-sources MemT 1.0 memory-native models, built with Nvidia
items.summary: The family, including a 554B-parameter Pro model on Nemotron 3 Ultra, keeps long histories in a fixed-size state to cut long-context serving costs.

items.headline: Tencent releases Hy-MT3 translation models covering 102 languages
items.summary: The open models come in three sizes and expand language coverage from 38 in Hy-MT2.

items.headline: Amazon to acquire Decart's AI-optimisation tech and team, reportedly for $7.5bn
items.summary: The asset deal aims to run models more efficiently on Amazon's Trainium chips and is subject to approval.

items.headline: Marlowe raises a $277m seed round for AI inference infrastructure
items.summary: Its first site, running Etched chips, is due online in December. Other large seeds this week include Embo ($110m) and ex-xAI founders' Epochal ($100m).

items.headline: Meta's Alexandr Wang writes that 'superintelligence is arriving' and urges a different path
items.summary: In an X essay he warned that models may soon out-improve humans at self-improvement and said Meta delayed its Muse agent for safety.

items.headline: UN autonomous-weapons talks extended to 2028 without a commitment to binding rules
items.summary: 128 states agreed to two more years of drafting under the CCW, after roughly 13 years of talks.

items.headline: State AGs ask the bankruptcy court to reject the sale of Character.AI's platform and chats
items.summary: California's attorney general and others object to private user chats being sold, ahead of a Dec 1 auction.

items.headline: Trending: Hugging Face's pybot, lastbook and agy-fast lead agent-tooling repos
items.summary: Immortal-Protocols/lastbook (about 3.1k stars), INK-Q/agy-fast (1.3k) and huggingface/pybot (1.2k) topped daily trending lists, per the digest.
